questions.prompt: What bold promise will you make that sets the expectation for what the audience will achieve by the end of your presentation?
Who is this presentation for? What different audience segments fall into your webinar (e.g., 'those who already have a business' vs 'those just starting out')?
What bad habits or distractions will you call out in your Take Control slide, and how will you prove the value of paying full attention?
What bonus or incentive can you offer to hook the audience to stay until the end?
What one or two key achievements will you share to qualify yourself without being boastful?
What success stories of previous clients will you use for your Street Cred slide?
What will their dream scenario look like after implementing your strategies (Future Pacing)?
Can you craft a single One Sentence Persuasion statement that encourages dreams, justifies failures, allays fears, confirms suspicions, and throws rocks at enemies?

concepts.name: Bold Promise Slide
concepts.definition: Opening slide that sets the expectation for what the audience will achieve by the end of your presentation. Use your headline as the bold promise.

concepts.name: Who Is This For? Slide
concepts.definition: Clarifies how the presentation will benefit different audience segments by calling out each group and listing the specific benefits they'll receive no matter which bucket they fall into.

concepts.name: Take Control Slide
concepts.definition: Ensures you have their full attention by calling out bad habits (Slack, Facebook, YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, Instagram) and proving the value of the presentation in dollar terms (e.g., XXX/hour consultation rate) so they set time aside and eliminate distractions.

concepts.name: Hook To The End Slide
concepts.definition: Provides an incentive for the audience to stay until the end â€” typically a valuable bonus revealed at the end of the presentation. Can also be offered as a bonus on the registration page.

concepts.name: Qualify Yourself Slide
concepts.definition: Establishes your credibility without boasting. Share one or two key achievements, 3rd party awards, endorsements, or a quick history. Presents the promise they want to receive one day, but lifts others up instead of being boastful.

concepts.name: Street Cred Slide
concepts.definition: Shows examples of how you've helped OTHERS achieve success. Different from Qualify Yourself â€” these are success stories of previous clients. Can also be used as a reason to stay on the presentation.

concepts.name: Future Pacing Slide
concepts.definition: Helps the audience visualize their future success by describing their dream scenario â€” whether that's escaping pain or reaching desires and goals. Describe what their life could look like after implementing your strategies.

concepts.name: One Sentence Persuasion (Bonus)
concepts.definition: Blair Warren's formula: 'People will do anything for those who encourage their dreams, justify their failures, allay their fears, confirm their suspicions, and help them throw rocks at their enemies.' Craft a single POWER statement that weaves all five elements into the introduction. (Allay = diminish or put at rest one's fears, suspicions or worries.)

questions.prompt: What are the false beliefs your audience has about your product/service / your 'map' to success?
What experiences caused these false beliefs?
What story/stories do they tell themselves to reinforce these beliefs?
What is the New Belief you need them to adopt (traditionally the opposite of the false belief)?
What is the story you can tell about realizing your 'success map' that will trump their limiting beliefs and stories?
What is your Backstory â€” the backstory that gives you a vested interest in your journey?
What are your Desires â€” what is it that you want to accomplish (External and Internal)?
What is The Wall â€” the wall/problem you hit within your current opportunity that started you on this new journey?
What was The Epiphany you experienced, and the new opportunity you discovered?
What is The Plan you created to achieve your desire?
What was The Conflict â€” what conflict did you experience along the way?
What was The Achievement â€” what was the end result that you achieved?
What was The Transformation that you experienced?

concepts.name: Chain of False Beliefs
concepts.definition: All customers carry a chain of false beliefs that hold them back. These beliefs are true to them based on their past experiences and the stories they've created. Identify them, describe the triggering experience, describe the reinforcing story, then define the NEW belief and the Epiphany Bridge Story that replaces the old one.

concepts.name: Belief-Breaking Story Sequence (5 Parts)
concepts.definition: 1) Identify their False Belief. 2) Describe their Past Experience that gave them this belief. 3) Describe their Story (what they tell themselves). 4) Define the New Epiphany Bridge Story they can adopt. 5) Describe how the New Belief allowed them to succeed.

concepts.name: Epiphany Bridge Story
concepts.definition: A script that takes someone through the hero's journey â€” telling your story in a way that creates an emotional response and bridges the gap from fear to belief. Moves from Emotion (Ah-ha / Epiphany) to Logic (Techno Babble) via 8 elements.

concepts.name: 8 Elements of a Correctly Presented Epiphany Bridge Story
concepts.definition: 1) The Backstory â€” vested interest in your journey. 2) Your Desires â€” External (struggle) and Internal (struggle). 3) The Wall â€” the wall/problem that started this new journey. 4) The Epiphany â€” the epiphany and new opportunity discovered. 5) The Plan â€” the plan to achieve your desire. 6) The Conflict â€” conflict experienced along the way. 7) The Achievement â€” end result achieved. 8) The Transformation â€” transformation experienced.

concepts.name: Emotion to Logic Bridge
concepts.definition: A properly built epiphany bridge hands the listener an emotional Ah-ha (epiphany) on the left side of the bridge, which gives them permission to accept the logical, technical details (techno babble) on the right side of the bridge.

exercises.name: Write Your Epiphany Bridge Story Workshop
exercises.prompt: Using the 8 Epiphany Bridge elements, write out your story with one text-box per element: The Backstory, Your Desires (External & Internal), The Wall, The Epiphany, The Plan, The Conflict, The Achievement, The Transformation.

concepts.name: Session Time Architecture
concepts.definition: First 5 minutes: Introduction and street cred. Next 15 minutes: your origin story of discovering the framework. NEXT 15 minutes: teaching the framework itself. Session #3 is where you deliver the VALUABLE CONTENT your audience came to learn.

concepts.name: Map As Framework #1
concepts.definition: Your origin-story map IS Framework #1 (Secret #1). Session #3 converts that map into a taught framework â€” the first of the three belief-shifting secrets in the Perfect Webinar.

concepts.name: Teaching Formula: Story, Strategy, Skip Tactics, Social Proof
concepts.definition: Most people make mistakes teaching their framework, leading to ineffective webinars. Correct order: 1) Story of Learning or Earning â€” start with a story about how you learned or earned the framework (builds credibility and sets the stage). 2) Teach the Strategy â€” explain the overall strategy behind your framework; strategy = WHAT needs to be done. 3) Teach the Strategy (HOW) â€” but SKIP the step-by-step how-to in your sales presentation; tactics = HOW to do it in your paid product. 4) Provide Social Proof â€” share examples or testimonials showing your framework works.

concepts.name: Strategy vs. Tactics Line
concepts.definition: Strategy = the WHAT (keep it in the webinar â€” this is what they paid attention for). Tactics = the HOW / step-by-step (save it for your paid offer). Teaching tactics in the free presentation is the #1 reason webinars fail to convert.

concepts.name: Slides-as-Visual-Cues (Reinforced)
concepts.definition: Slides in the framework section also serve the presenter. Each slide represents a key point or STRATEGY in the framework. They help you remember the flow; they are not walls of text for the audience to read.

Social Proof: Share success stories of people who used funnel hacking to achieve great results.
